correctness_confidence.basis: Complete text and targeted source reading found no invalidation of a principal theorem. Section 29 calculations and quantifiers were checked analytically. No independent formal rebuild or full dependency audit was performed.

rigor.basis: Explicit finite-dimensional proofs, constants, kernel conditions and counterexamples make the central arguments inspectable. Threshold-equality wording and an overly exhaustive methodological conclusion need correction.

novelty.basis: The discrete weighted adapters and section 29 separation examples are plausible original contributions. Core Fourier, rank, Schur, Cwikel, partition and path-comparison tools are classical; exhaustive priority is unverified.

significance.basis: Substantive finite obstructions and positive families clarify a constrained programme. The generic critical rectangular problem remains open, and no interacting continuum or Millennium solution follows.

reproducibility.basis: The exact PDF and all 81 supplied manifest entries matched hashes; text, source and renders support inspection. Colab and formal evidence were read, not independently rerun; same-source clones do not establish independent proof replication.

summary: Single fresh assessment of the exact 63-page v8 PDF: 4.20/10, rounded to 4 overall stars (Strong), with minor revisions recommended for this Working paper. This is a research-position rating, not a correctness probability or criterion average. No principal mathematical claim was invalidated in this reading. Retain threshold-convention, methodological-overstatement and lineage corrections, and all reproducibility, priority and continuum limitations. The reviewer has historical ancestor-review context in the same orchestrated account/chat; this is not blind or organizationally independent and is not human peer review. The configured model label is not served-backend attestation; backend identity and reasoning effort were not exposed. See scientific-review.md for the complete findings and evidence scope.
strengths: Explicit Fourier-band dimension and rank-nullity arguments separate arbitrary measurements from bounded-rank sectors and preserve uniform quantifiers.
The manuscript carefully distinguishes finite rank obstructions, physical scaling, nonlinear/differentiable hypotheses and open continuum extensions.

Section 29 supplies useful distinctions: mean-zero low-rank graph obstructions, sampled coexact fields, a bounded two-scale positive family, local bypass coercivity and a sparse weak-site certificate obstruction.
The section 29 path comparison and minimum-coefficient counterexample have direct, inspectable calculations; the paper expressly distinguishes the nonlocal example from local lattice energies.
weaknesses: F4: Formal/replay assurance is incomplete in this review. No independent Lean rebuild, dependency closure or scientific rerun was performed. Finite tests and clones using the same code are not independent verification of universal theorems.

F5: Priority is not established beyond qualified candidates. Much of the machinery is classical; targeted checks of Frank, Diaconis-Saloff-Coste and de Berg do not amount to exhaustive literature verification.
F6: The generic critical rectangular problem remains open. These finite results do not construct an interacting continuum theory, establish a physical mass gap, or resolve a Millennium problem.

F7: The 63-page dossier contains a long abstract and repeated runtime/history material. A theorem/scope table and a separate evidence appendix would improve scientific readability without discarding objections.
potential_errors: F1, p.59, section 29.3 final paragraph: the phrase at or above b about mandated singletons conflicts with the earlier strict a<tau isolation convention at tau=b. Use tau<=b for the mesh branch and tau>b for the singleton branch, or explicitly change the convention. The mesh argument covers equality; this does not invalidate the theorem.

F2, p.62 final paragraph before references: the statement that the next positive mechanism must use actual weighted local energy or capacity suggests an exhaustive necessity theorem not proved here. Recast as a research recommendation and limitation of the specific tested methods, not a classification of all possible proofs or hybrids.

F3, p.21 versus pp.44-45: immediate-predecessor wording referring to v5 conflicts with the identified v7 parent. Label the older historical comparison explicitly or update lineage wording. Related draft wording on p.55 should be clarified. This is a provenance/editorial issue, not a theorem failure.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact finite rectangular-mean Schur threshold in section 29.1 and its contrast with an arbitrary two-set partition may be useful; general low-rank obstruction principles are classical and priority is unverified.

The section 29.2 explicit coexact sample-erasure construction and dimension-dependent support lower bound are plausible specialized contributions, with its changing physical scale explicitly retained.

The section 29.4-29.5 combination of local bypass coercivity and diverging minimum-coefficient-certified partition cost isolates a useful failure of that certificate class; comparison methods themselves are classical.
